thesis: DoubleVerify was flat at $13.615 (from $13.60) on 8.3x volume in Friday's half-day session, 0.3% under its 52-week high and just above the $13.60 per-share cash price in its agreement to be acquired by Neptune BidCo US, a Nielsen affiliate, signed Aug 6, 2026 (8-K): about $2.15B of enterprise value, backed by a $200M Elliott equity commitment and about $1.8B of committed debt. Stockholders approved on Oct 29, and closing is expected by Q1 2027, subject to Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance, which this run found no confirmation of; one account gives an initial outside date of May 6, 2027. With the shares at or slightly above the fixed cash price, no spread remains, and this run found no company disclosure explaining today's volume. The litigation check found a 2025 securities class action in the S.D.N.Y. (No. 25-cv-04332, alleging undisclosed customer shifts away from open exchanges) and a December 2025 derivative suit, with no scheduled step found, plus plaintiff-firm reviews of the deal price, and no restatement. Medium; avoid.
invalidation: The merger agreement is terminated, antitrust review blocks or conditions the deal, or a competing proposal above $13.60 emerges.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22 on the Oct 21 proposal; a third sold at the +8% take-profit tier on Nov 24). ROIV rose about 2.4% to $43.23 (from $42.20) in Friday's half-day session, setting a 52-week high of $43.28 intraday and closing 0.1% below it; this run found no company disclosure dated after the fiscal Q2 release (company release). This run's searches confirmed the FDA's priority review of brepocitinib in dermatomyositis (accepted March 2026) and that IMVT-1402 at 600 mg met its primary endpoint in a late-line rheumatoid arthritis study. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis stay open: the uveitis data are not an approval, the batoclimab Phase 3 miss shows pipeline risk, and early launch revenue was flattered by specialty-pharmacy stocking. The litigation check found the Federal Circuit appeal in Arbutus v. Moderna (No. 26-1581), argued Nov 5, still undecided, with up to $1.3B of additional payment riding on an affirmance and no decision date set, and no restatement. This stays medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls once stocking unwinds, FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or the Federal Circuit rules for Moderna and removes the contingent payment.
sources: Knobbe Martens (Federal Circuit argument Nov 5, decision awaited): https://www.knobbe.com/?p=67318

IAM (Federal Circuit to consider government-contractor liability): https://www.iam-media.com/article/federal-circuit-consider-scope-of-patent-infringement-liability-government-contractors-in-moderna-vaccine-dispute

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 19 on the Nov 18 proposal). H World rose about 1.8% to $52.65 (from $51.73) in Friday's half-day session, about 1.1% above the $52.06 fill and 7.0% below its 52-week high; this run found no company disclosure dated after its Q3 2026 release (company release), which reported 14,026 hotels and 1,381,324 rooms in operation at Sept 30, 2026. The Aug 17 Q2 release had raised 2026 revenue growth guidance and announced a new shareholder return plan. The counter-case named in the prior thesis stays open: same-hotel RevPAR fell 4.4% in Q3. The litigation check found a February 2026 Beijing Consumers Association summons over a mandatory-arbitration clause in its membership terms, and a 2020 plaintiff-firm investigation of the predecessor Huazhu Group that followed a short-seller report, with no filed suit, scheduled step or restatement found. The early-exit guard still applies (opened 5 trading days ago, the last day of its window), and no fact newer than the entry thesis was found. This stays medium.
invalidation: Same-hotel RevPAR declines deepen, the raised revenue guidance is cut, or the shares give back the post-report gain.
